cards.didYouKnow: A group of lions is called a pride.
facts: A lion's roar can be heard up to 8 km away.
Lions sleep up to 20 hours a day!
cards.front: Who is called the King of the Jungle?

cards.didYouKnow: Penguins cannot fly, but they are amazing swimmers.
facts: Penguins slide on their bellies on ice — it is called tobogganing.
Emperor penguins are the tallest, about 1.1 metres tall.
cards.front: Which bird cannot fly but loves to swim?

cards.didYouKnow: It uses its trunk like a hand to pick up food.
facts: An elephant's trunk has about 40,000 muscles!
Elephants can hear with their feet — they feel rumbles in the ground.
cards.front: Which is the largest land animal?

cards.didYouKnow: Butterflies taste their food with their feet.
facts: A butterfly starts life as a caterpillar.
The Monarch butterfly can fly 4,000 km on migration!
cards.front: Which insect tastes with its feet?

cards.didYouKnow: Cheetahs cannot roar like lions — they chirp and purr like a house cat.
facts: A cheetah can run up to 100 km per hour — faster than a car on a city road!
It can go from 0 to 100 km per hour in about 3 seconds.
cards.front: Which land animal is the fastest runner?

cards.didYouKnow: An octopus has 3 hearts, and two of them stop beating when it swims!
facts: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
They can change colour and squeeze through a gap as small as a coin.
cards.front: Which sea animal has three hearts?
Which is the tallest land animal?
facts: A giraffe's long neck helps it eat leaves from the tops of tall trees.
A giraffe has the same number of neck bones as you — seven!
cards.didYouKnow: A giraffe's tongue is dark blue and can be about half a metre long!

cards.front: Which big cat has black stripes on orange fur?
facts: A tiger is the biggest cat in the world.
No two tigers have the same stripes — just like your fingerprints.
cards.didYouKnow: Tigers love water and are very good swimmers!

cards.front: Which animal carries its baby in a pouch?
facts: A baby kangaroo is called a joey and lives in its mother's pouch.
Kangaroos hop on two strong back legs and use their tail to balance.
cards.didYouKnow: A kangaroo cannot walk backwards easily!

cards.front: Which animal sleeps in a tree and eats eucalyptus leaves?
facts: Koalas eat eucalyptus leaves and almost nothing else.
A koala is not a bear at all — it is a marsupial, like a kangaroo.
cards.didYouKnow: A koala can sleep for up to 20 hours a day!

cards.front: Which black and white animal eats bamboo all day?
facts: Giant pandas live in the mountains of China.
They eat bamboo for most of the day — it is almost all they eat.
cards.didYouKnow: A giant panda has an extra thumb-like bone that helps it hold bamboo!

cards.front: Which white bear lives in the snowy Arctic?
facts: Polar bears live in the cold Arctic, around the North Pole.
They are wonderful swimmers and can swim for many kilometres.
cards.didYouKnow: A polar bear's fur looks white, but each hair is actually see-through!

cards.front: Which animal wears black and white stripes?
facts: Zebras live in Africa in big groups called herds.
A zebra's stripes help confuse lions that try to hunt it.
cards.didYouKnow: No two zebras have the same stripe pattern!

cards.front: Which is the biggest ape in the world?
facts: Gorillas live in the forests of Africa.
They mostly eat plants, leaves and fruit.
cards.didYouKnow: Male gorillas beat their chests to show how strong they are!

cards.front: Which sea animal is very clever and loves to play?
facts: Dolphins live in groups called pods and talk with clicks and whistles.
They are mammals, so they breathe air through a hole on top of their head.
cards.didYouKnow: A dolphin can sleep with one eye open and half of its brain awake!

cards.front: Which is the biggest animal that has ever lived?
facts: A blue whale can grow longer than 30 metres — longer than three buses!
It eats tiny sea animals called krill, even though it is so huge.
cards.didYouKnow: A blue whale's heart is as big as a small car!

cards.front: Which sea animal has rows of sharp teeth?
facts: Sharks have a wonderful sense of smell and can smell a drop of blood in the sea.
If a shark loses a tooth, a new one grows in its place.
cards.didYouKnow: A shark can grow thousands of teeth in its whole life!

cards.front: Which bird hunts at night with big eyes?
facts: Owls hunt at night and have very big eyes to see in the dark.
They fly almost silently, so their prey cannot hear them coming.
cards.didYouKnow: An owl can turn its head almost all the way around!

cards.front: Which bird has the sharpest eyes in the sky?
facts: An eagle can spot a small animal from very high in the sky.
Its strong wings help it soar for hours without flapping much.
cards.didYouKnow: The bald eagle is the national bird of the United States of America!

cards.front: Which tiny bird can fly backwards?
facts: Hummingbirds flap their wings many times every second.
They drink sweet nectar from flowers with their long beaks.
cards.didYouKnow: A hummingbird is so small that some weigh less than a coin!

cards.front: Which pink bird stands on one leg?
facts: Flamingos often stand on one leg while they rest.
They eat in the water with their heads held upside down.
cards.didYouKnow: A flamingo gets its pink colour from the food it eats — baby flamingos are born grey!

cards.front: Which lizard can change its colour?
facts: A chameleon can change its colour to hide or to show how it feels.
Its two eyes can move in different directions at the same time.
cards.didYouKnow: A chameleon's tongue is very long and sticky — it shoots out to catch insects!

cards.front: Which animal has no legs but moves very fast?
facts: A snake smells with its forked tongue, which picks up tiny bits from the air.
Snakes shed their skin as they grow bigger.
cards.didYouKnow: Some snakes can go for months without eating!

cards.front: Which animal starts life as a tadpole?
facts: A baby frog is called a tadpole and lives in water.
Frogs can live both in water and on land.
cards.didYouKnow: Some frogs can jump 20 times their own body length!

cards.front: Which animal carries its home on its back?
facts: A tortoise carries a hard shell on its back for safety.
It moves slowly but can live for a very, very long time.
cards.didYouKnow: Some giant tortoises live for more than 100 years!

cards.front: Which desert animal has a hump on its back?
facts: A camel's hump stores fat, which gives it energy in the desert.
Its long eyelashes keep sand out of its eyes.
cards.didYouKnow: A camel can go for many days without drinking water!

cards.front: Which animal can sleep standing up?
facts: Horses can sleep standing up, and they can also lie down to rest.
They eat grass and hay, and love to run fast.
cards.didYouKnow: Horses have the biggest eyes of any land animal!

cards.front: Which animal is known as man's best friend?
facts: Dogs have a sense of smell that is far better than ours.
They wag their tails when they are happy or excited.
cards.didYouKnow: A dog's nose print is unique — just like your fingerprint!

cards.front: Which pet purrs when it is happy?
facts: Cats purr when they are happy and relaxed.
They can see very well in the dark.
cards.didYouKnow: A cat's whiskers help it feel its way in the dark and judge small spaces!

cards.front: Which is the only mammal that can truly fly?
facts: Bats sleep hanging upside down during the day.
They use echoes to find food in the dark — this is called echolocation.
cards.didYouKnow: There are more than 1,400 kinds of bats in the world!

A day on Mars is about 24 hours and 37 minutes.

cards.didYouKnow: Saturn is so light it would float in water!
facts: Its rings are made of ice and rock.
Saturn has more than 140 moons.
cards.front: Which planet wears beautiful rings?

cards.didYouKnow: A day on Jupiter is the shortest of all planets — only about 10 hours long!
facts: Jupiter is the biggest planet — more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.
Its Great Red Spot is a giant storm bigger than Earth that has raged for hundreds of years.

cards.didYouKnow: Astronauts on the space station see 16 sunrises and sunsets every single day!
facts: Astronauts live and work on the space station, floating high above Earth.
It goes all the way around Earth in about 90 minutes, and it is as big as a football field.
cards.front: Where do astronauts live in space?
Which is the hottest planet in our solar system?
facts: Venus is covered in thick clouds that trap heat.
It spins backwards, unlike most other planets.
cards.didYouKnow: Venus is so bright that people call it the Morning Star!

cards.front: Which is the smallest planet in our solar system?
facts: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
A year on Mercury lasts only 88 days.
cards.didYouKnow: Mercury is very hot in the daytime and freezing cold at night!

cards.front: Which is the only planet we know that has life?
facts: About 70 percent of Earth is covered by water.
Earth has only one Moon.
cards.didYouKnow: Earth is the only planet that is not named after a god!

cards.front: Which planet is the farthest from the Sun?
facts: Neptune is a deep blue planet, and its colour comes from a gas called methane.
It takes Neptune about 165 years to go around the Sun once.
cards.didYouKnow: Neptune has the fastest winds of any planet!

cards.front: Which planet spins on its side like a rolling ball?
facts: Uranus spins on its side, unlike other planets.
Its blue-green colour comes from a gas called methane.
cards.didYouKnow: Uranus is one of the coldest planets in the solar system!

cards.front: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
facts: Neil Armstrong walked on the Moon in 1969.
He travelled there in a spacecraft called Apollo 11.
cards.didYouKnow: His first words on the Moon were, 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind!'

cards.front: What takes astronauts up into space?
facts: A rocket burns fuel to push itself up into the sky.
Rockets carry astronauts and satellites into space.
cards.didYouKnow: A rocket needs huge power to escape the pull of Earth's gravity!

cards.front: What icy visitor grows a glowing tail near the Sun?
facts: A comet is a ball of ice and dust that travels around the Sun.
When it comes near the Sun, it grows a bright, glowing tail.
cards.didYouKnow: Halley's Comet visits our skies about every 75 years!

cards.front: What are the rocky pieces that float between Mars and Jupiter?
facts: Asteroids are rocky pieces left over from when the planets were formed.
Most of them live in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
cards.didYouKnow: Some asteroids are as big as mountains!

cards.front: What do we call a 'shooting star'?
facts: A meteor is a space rock that burns brightly as it falls through the sky.
If a piece lands on Earth, we call it a meteorite.
cards.didYouKnow: Most meteors burn up completely before they reach the ground!

cards.front: What is a star made of?
cards.answer: A Giant Ball of Hot Gas!
facts: A star is a giant ball of hot gas that gives out light and heat.
The Sun is a star — it is just the closest one to us.
cards.didYouKnow: Stars look like they twinkle because of the air moving around Earth!

cards.front: What is the name of our galaxy?
facts: Our galaxy is called the Milky Way.
It holds billions of stars, and our Sun is one of them.
cards.didYouKnow: On a dark night, the Milky Way looks like a milky band of light across the sky!

cards.front: What has gravity so strong that even light cannot escape?
facts: A black hole is made when a very big star dies.
Its gravity is so strong that not even light can escape from it.
cards.didYouKnow: We cannot see a black hole directly — scientists find it by watching the stars around it!

cards.front: Who travels and works in space?
facts: Astronauts wear special suits that give them air to breathe.
In space they float, because there is almost no gravity.
cards.didYouKnow: Astronauts eat their food from special packets in space!

cards.front: What helps our TVs, maps and weather forecasts from space?
facts: A satellite is a machine that goes around Earth in space.
Satellites help us with TV, maps, phone calls and weather forecasts.
cards.didYouKnow: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite!

cards.front: What do we use to see faraway stars and planets?
facts: A telescope makes faraway things in the sky look closer.
The Hubble telescope floats in space and takes wonderful photos.
cards.didYouKnow: More than 400 years ago, Galileo used a telescope to spot four moons of Jupiter!

cards.front: What happens when the Moon covers the Sun?
facts: During a solar eclipse, the Moon moves between Earth and the Sun.
The sky can go dark in the middle of the day.
cards.didYouKnow: Never look at the Sun directly, even during an eclipse — it can hurt your eyes!

cards.front: What happens when Earth's shadow falls on the Moon?
facts: During a lunar eclipse, Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon.
The Moon can turn a deep red colour — people call it a blood moon.
cards.didYouKnow: A lunar eclipse can last for hours, and it is safe to watch with your eyes!

cards.front: How many planets go around the Sun?
facts: Eight planets travel around the Sun in our solar system.
Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
cards.didYouKnow: The Sun holds more than 99 percent of all the stuff in our solar system!

cards.front: What do we call a group of stars that makes a picture?
facts: A constellation is a group of stars that looks like a picture in the sky.
Long ago, sailors used constellations to find their way at sea.
cards.didYouKnow: The Big Dipper looks like a big spoon in the sky!

cards.front: What robot drives around on Mars?
facts: A Mars rover is a robot that drives on the surface of Mars.
It takes photos and sends them back to Earth.
cards.didYouKnow: The rover Perseverance landed on Mars in 2021 and is still exploring!

cards.front: Which tiny world used to be called a planet?
facts: Pluto used to be called the ninth planet.
Now scientists call it a dwarf planet.
cards.didYouKnow: Pluto is even smaller than our Moon!

cards.front: Why does the Moon change shape in the sky?
facts: The Moon looks different as it moves around Earth — crescent, half and full.
A full moon is round and bright in the night sky.
cards.didYouKnow: It takes the Moon about a month to go through all its shapes!

cards.front: Why do we have day and night?
facts: Earth spins around once every day, in 24 hours.
The side facing the Sun has day, while the other side has night.
cards.didYouKnow: Earth spins so fast that places on the equator move at more than 1,600 km every hour!

cards.didYouKnow: The Colosseum is the biggest amphitheatre ever built — and it is still standing after nearly 2,000 years!
facts: The Colosseum stands in Rome, Italy, and was built almost 2,000 years ago.
It could hold about 50,000 people, and gladiators fought there long ago.
cards.front: Which giant round building in Rome did gladiators fight in?

cards.didYouKnow: Some sand dunes in the Sahara are taller than a 30-storey building!
facts: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, about the size of the USA.
Thousands of years ago, the Sahara was green, with lakes and rivers.
cards.front: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
Which is the tallest mountain in the world?
facts: Mount Everest is 8,849 metres tall.
It stands in the Himalayas, on the border of Nepal and China.
cards.didYouKnow: Mount Everest grows a little taller every year!

cards.front: Which white marble wonder stands in Agra, India?
facts: The Taj Mahal is made of shining white marble.
Emperor Shah Jahan built it for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
cards.didYouKnow: It took about 20 years to build the Taj Mahal!

cards.front: Which is the largest rainforest in the world?
facts: The Amazon is the largest rainforest in the world.
It is in South America and is home to more kinds of plants and animals than almost anywhere else on Earth.
cards.didYouKnow: The Amazon is often called the 'lungs of the Earth' because it makes so much oxygen!

cards.front: Which famous waterfalls are between the USA and Canada?
facts: Niagara Falls is made of three waterfalls.
The water falls from about 50 metres high.
cards.didYouKnow: Millions of people visit Niagara Falls every year!

cards.front: What is the name of the great bell in London?
facts: Big Ben is the great bell in a clock tower in London.
The tower stands beside the River Thames.
cards.didYouKnow: Big Ben has been ringing for more than 160 years!

cards.front: Which famous tower in Italy leans to one side?
facts: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is a bell tower in Italy.
It started to lean while it was being built, more than 800 years ago.
cards.didYouKnow: Builders tried to fix the lean, but the tower still leans today!

cards.front: Which famous building looks like white sails?
facts: The Sydney Opera House stands in Sydney, Australia.
Its roof looks like the sails of ships.
cards.didYouKnow: The Sydney Opera House opened in 1973!

cards.front: Which is the tallest mountain in Japan?
facts: Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan.
It is a volcano with snow on its top.
cards.didYouKnow: Mount Fuji is a symbol of Japan and appears in many paintings!

cards.front: Which huge canyon was carved by a river in the USA?
facts: The Grand Canyon is in Arizona, in the United States.
The Colorado River carved it over millions of years.
cards.didYouKnow: The Grand Canyon is about 446 km long — longer than 4,000 football fields!

cards.front: What are the colourful lights that dance in the northern sky?
facts: The Northern Lights are colourful lights in the night sky.
They are seen near the North Pole, in places like Norway and Iceland.
cards.didYouKnow: The lights are made by tiny bits from the Sun hitting the air around Earth!

cards.front: Which is the largest coral reef in the world?
facts: The Great Barrier Reef lies in the sea near Australia.
It is home to many colourful fish, turtles and corals.
cards.didYouKnow: The Great Barrier Reef is so big that it can be seen from space!

cards.front: Which is the coldest continent on Earth?
facts: Antarctica is covered in ice and snow all year.
Penguins live there, but no people live there all the time.
cards.didYouKnow: No country owns Antarctica — it belongs to everyone for science and peace!

cards.front: Which river helped the ancient Egyptians grow food?
facts: The River Nile flows through Egypt in Africa.
It flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.
cards.didYouKnow: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world!

cards.front: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
facts: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
It covers more of Earth than all the land put together.
cards.didYouKnow: The deepest place on Earth, the Mariana Trench, is in the Pacific Ocean!

cards.front: In which sea can people float without trying?
facts: The Dead Sea is so salty that people float easily on it.
It lies between Jordan and Israel.
cards.didYouKnow: The Dead Sea is the lowest place on land on Earth!

cards.front: Which is the tallest mountain in Africa?
facts: Mount Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania, in Africa.
It has snow on its top, even though it is near the equator.
cards.didYouKnow: Mount Kilimanjaro is a sleeping volcano that has not erupted for thousands of years!

cards.front: Which lost city of the Incas hides in the mountains of Peru?
facts: Machu Picchu is an old Inca city high in the mountains of Peru.
It was built about 600 years ago.
cards.didYouKnow: The stones of Machu Picchu fit together so well that no cement was needed!

cards.front: Which is the largest religious monument in the world?
facts: Angkor Wat is a huge temple in Cambodia.
It was built about 900 years ago, first as a Hindu temple.
cards.didYouKnow: Angkor Wat is so big that it has five towers shaped like lotus flowers!

cards.front: Which giant stones stand in a circle in England?
facts: Stonehenge is a circle of giant stones in England.
It was built about 5,000 years ago.
cards.didYouKnow: Nobody knows exactly how people moved the giant stones to Stonehenge!

cards.front: Which is the tallest building in the world?
facts: The Burj Khalifa stands in Dubai.
It is 828 metres tall and has more than 160 floors.
cards.didYouKnow: On a clear day, you can see very far from the top of the Burj Khalifa!

cards.front: Which orange-red bridge stands in San Francisco?
facts: The Golden Gate Bridge is in San Francisco, in the United States.
It opened in 1937 and is painted orange-red.
cards.didYouKnow: The Golden Gate Bridge is so long that it took four years to build!

cards.front: Which huge waterfall is in Africa?
facts: Victoria Falls is on the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe in Africa.
It is one of the largest waterfalls in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: The local name for Victoria Falls means 'the smoke that thunders'!

cards.front: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
facts: Lake Baikal is in Russia.
It is the deepest lake in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: Lake Baikal holds about one-fifth of all the fresh water on Earth!

cards.front: Which giant statue opens its arms over Rio de Janeiro?
facts: Christ the Redeemer is a giant statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
It stands on top of a mountain with its arms stretched wide.
cards.didYouKnow: The statue is 38 metres tall, as tall as a 12-storey building!

facts: Lava is melted rock hotter than 1,000°C.

cards.didYouKnow: The Earth itself is like a giant magnet.
facts: Magnets have a north pole and a south pole.
Opposite poles attract, same poles push away.

cards.didYouKnow: Bees dance to tell other bees where flowers are.
facts: One bee makes only about half a teaspoon of honey in its whole life.
A hive can have up to 60,000 bees!
cards.front: Which tiny insect makes honey?

cards.didYouKnow: Your heart beats about 100,000 times a day — that is about 3 billion times in a lifetime!
facts: Your heart is about the size of your fist and pumps blood all around your body.
It beats about 100,000 times every single day, even while you sleep.
cards.front: Which part of your body pumps blood all day and night?

cards.didYouKnow: A bolt of lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun!
facts: Lightning is a huge spark of electricity in the sky during a storm.
We see lightning before we hear thunder because light travels faster than sound.
cards.front: What flash of light do we see in the sky during a storm?
How does rain get back up into the sky?
facts: Water from seas and rivers rises up as tiny drops called vapour.
The vapour cools and makes clouds, and then it falls as rain.
cards.didYouKnow: The same water you drink today may have fallen as rain long, long ago!

cards.front: How do plants make their own food?
facts: Leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food for the plant.
Plants give out oxygen, which we need to breathe.
cards.didYouKnow: The green colour in leaves comes from a substance called chlorophyll!

cards.front: How many bones are in an adult human body?
facts: Adults have 206 bones in their bodies.
Babies are born with about 300 bones, and some join together as they grow.
cards.didYouKnow: Bones protect soft parts inside you, like your brain and heart!

cards.front: Which part of your body helps you think and learn?
facts: Your brain controls everything you do, even while you sleep.
It is made of billions of tiny cells called neurons.
cards.didYouKnow: Your brain uses a lot of your body's energy, even when you are just thinking!

cards.front: Why do we have summer and winter?
facts: Earth leans to one side as it goes around the Sun.
The lean makes one part of Earth warmer while another part is colder.
cards.didYouKnow: When it is summer in India, it is winter in Australia!

cards.front: What pulls everything down to the ground?
facts: Gravity is the force that pulls everything down to the ground.
It also keeps the Moon going around Earth.
cards.didYouKnow: Without gravity, you would float away into space!

cards.front: What slows things down when they rub together?
facts: Friction is the force that slows things down when they rub against each other.
Ice has very little friction, which is why we slip on it.
cards.didYouKnow: Rub your hands together fast — friction makes them feel warm!

cards.front: What travels in waves that our ears can hear?
facts: Sound travels in waves through air, water and even solids.
Sound travels faster in water than it does in air.
cards.didYouKnow: Sound cannot travel in space, because there is no air there!

cards.front: What is the fastest thing in the whole universe?
facts: Light travels about 300,000 km every single second.
It is the fastest thing we know in the universe.
cards.didYouKnow: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth!

cards.front: What powers our lights, fans and TVs?
facts: Electricity is a form of energy that powers things in our homes.
Lightning is a huge spark of electricity in the sky.
cards.didYouKnow: Never touch electric wires — electricity can be dangerous!

cards.front: Who made the first long-lasting light bulb?
facts: Thomas Edison made the first light bulb that could shine for a long time.
A light bulb changes electricity into light.
cards.didYouKnow: New LED bulbs use much less power than old bulbs!

cards.front: What do doctors use to check if you have a fever?
facts: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is.
A healthy person's body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius.
cards.didYouKnow: The first thermometers were made more than 400 years ago!

cards.front: What do scientists use to see tiny germs?
facts: A microscope makes tiny things look much bigger.
Scientists use it to see germs and tiny living things.
cards.didYouKnow: A single drop of water can hold thousands of tiny living things!

cards.front: What tiny living things can make us sick?
facts: Germs are tiny living things that we cannot see with our eyes.
Some germs can make us sick.
cards.didYouKnow: Washing your hands with soap removes germs and keeps you healthy!

cards.front: Which part of your body churns your food?
facts: Food travels from your mouth to your stomach through a tube.
Your stomach churns the food and mixes it with juices that break it down.
cards.didYouKnow: Your stomach makes acid that is strong enough to help melt food!

cards.front: Which parts of your body help you breathe?
facts: Your lungs take in oxygen from the air you breathe.
When you breathe out, your lungs push out a gas called carbon dioxide.
cards.didYouKnow: You breathe about 20,000 times every day!

cards.front: How many teeth do adults have?
facts: Adults have 32 teeth.
Babies have 20 milk teeth, which fall out as they grow.
cards.didYouKnow: Brush your teeth twice a day to keep them strong and healthy!

cards.front: What helps your body move?
facts: Muscles help your body move, run, jump and smile.
You have hundreds of muscles in your body.
cards.didYouKnow: Your heart is a muscle too — and it never gets tired!

cards.front: What red liquid flows through your body?
facts: Blood carries oxygen to every part of your body.
Your heart pumps blood all around your body.
cards.didYouKnow: An adult's body has about 5 litres of blood!

cards.front: How many senses do we have?
facts: We have five senses: seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching.
Our eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin help us use them.
cards.didYouKnow: Your senses help you learn about the world around you!

cards.front: What does a seed need to grow into a plant?
facts: A seed needs water, air and sunlight to grow.
When a seed grows, its roots come out first and go down into the soil.
cards.didYouKnow: Some seeds can grow into trees that live for hundreds of years!

cards.front: Which animal has eight legs and spins webs?
facts: A spider has eight legs and spins silk webs.
It is not an insect — insects have only six legs.
cards.didYouKnow: Most spiders are not dangerous to people at all!

cards.front: Which tiny insect can carry things much heavier than itself?
facts: Ants live in big groups called colonies.
They follow smell trails to find food and to find their way home.
cards.didYouKnow: An ant can carry things many times heavier than its own body!

cards.front: Which wiggly animal has no eyes and helps the soil?
facts: An earthworm has no eyes.
It helps make the soil healthy for plants to grow.
cards.didYouKnow: An earthworm breathes through its skin!

facts: It is the most popular sport in the world.
A football match lasts 90 minutes.
cards.front: Which sport is played with a round ball and feet?

cards.didYouKnow: The world's longest pizza was over 1.8 km long!
facts: The first pizzas were made in Naples, Italy.
October is National Pizza Month in the USA.

cards.didYouKnow: Chocolate was once used as money by the Aztecs.
facts: Cocoa beans grow on trees in warm countries.
White chocolate is not really chocolate — it has no cocoa solids.
cards.front: Which sweet treat comes from cocoa beans?

cards.didYouKnow: The Olympic rings stand for the five inhabited continents.
facts: They happen every 4 years.
The first modern Olympics were in Athens in 1896.
cards.front: Which games bring athletes from all over the world?

cards.didYouKnow: The longest cricket match ever lasted 12 days — and it still ended in a draw!
facts: Cricket is played with a bat, a hard ball and wickets.
A cricket team has 11 players, and it is one of the most popular sports in India.
cards.front: Which sport is played with a bat, a ball and wickets?

cards.didYouKnow: It takes about 50 licks to finish one scoop of ice cream!
facts: The first ice cream shop in America opened in New York in 1776.
Vanilla is the most popular ice cream flavour in the world.
cards.front: Which cold, sweet treat comes in a cone?
Which sport is played with a racket and a ball over a net?
facts: In tennis, players hit a ball over a net with a racket.
Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: In tennis, a score of zero is called 'love'!

cards.front: Which sport do you play by throwing a ball through a hoop?
facts: In basketball, players throw the ball through a high hoop.
Each team has five players on the court.
cards.didYouKnow: A basket can be worth 2 or 3 points!

cards.front: Which sport uses a shuttlecock and a light racket?
facts: In badminton, players hit a shuttlecock over a net.
A shuttlecock is made with feathers.
cards.didYouKnow: Badminton is one of the fastest racket sports in the world!

cards.front: Which sport is played with a stick and a hard ball?
facts: In hockey, players use sticks to hit a hard ball into a goal.
Hockey is a very popular sport in India.
cards.didYouKnow: India has won the most Olympic gold medals in hockey!

cards.front: Which sport has freestyle, backstroke and butterfly?
facts: Swimming has four main strokes: freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.
Swimming is wonderful exercise for your whole body.
cards.didYouKnow: Michael Phelps has won 23 Olympic gold medals in swimming — more than anyone else!

cards.front: How long is a marathon race?
facts: A marathon is a very long race of about 42 km.
It is named after a place called Marathon in Greece.
cards.didYouKnow: Marathon runners train for many months before the race!

cards.front: Which race is the most famous bicycle race in the world?
facts: The Tour de France is the most famous bicycle race in the world.
It lasts about three weeks.
cards.didYouKnow: Cyclists in the Tour de France ride more than 3,000 km!

cards.front: Which sport has flips, jumps and the balance beam?
facts: Gymnasts do flips, jumps and balances.
The balance beam is only 10 cm wide — as wide as your hand.
cards.didYouKnow: Gymnasts need both strength and balance to perform!

cards.front: Which board game is called the game of kings?
facts: Chess is a board game for two players.
The king is the most important piece — if it is trapped, the game is over.
cards.didYouKnow: Chess began in India long, long ago!

cards.front: Which team sport from India has players chanting 'kabaddi'?
facts: Kabaddi is a team sport that began in India.
Each team has seven players on the court.
cards.didYouKnow: In kabaddi, the raider chants 'kabaddi, kabaddi' without stopping for breath!

cards.front: Which sport has six players on each side of a high net?
facts: In volleyball, players hit the ball over a high net.
Each team has six players on the court.
cards.didYouKnow: In volleyball, players must not let the ball touch the ground on their side!

cards.front: Which sport is played with a bat and four bases?
facts: In baseball, players hit the ball with a bat and run around four bases.
Baseball is very popular in the United States and Japan.
cards.didYouKnow: A baseball game has nine innings!

cards.front: Which sport is played by hitting a small ball into holes?
facts: In golf, players hit a small ball into holes with clubs.
A normal round of golf has 18 holes.
cards.didYouKnow: In golf, the player with the fewest hits wins!

cards.front: Which sport do players fight in with gloves in a ring?
facts: In boxing, two players fight with gloves in a ring.
A boxing match is split into rounds.
cards.didYouKnow: Boxers wear gloves to protect their hands and their opponent!

cards.front: Which martial art from Japan means 'empty hand'?
facts: Karate is a martial art that began in Japan.
Karate means 'empty hand' because fighters use no weapons.
cards.didYouKnow: In karate, belts show a student's level — from white to black!

cards.front: Which sport do you ride waves on a board?
facts: In surfing, people ride big waves on a board.
Hawaii is a famous place for surfing.
cards.didYouKnow: Surfers stand up on their boards as the wave carries them!

cards.front: Which yellow fruit grows in bunches and gives you quick energy?
facts: Bananas grow in bunches on a tall plant.
They give you quick energy, so they are a great snack for players.
cards.didYouKnow: Monkeys love bananas, but they eat many other fruits too!

cards.front: Which fruit is called the king of fruits?
facts: Mangoes are sweet summer fruits.
India grows more mangoes than any other country in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: There are hundreds of kinds of mangoes!

cards.front: Which fruit comes in red, green and yellow?
facts: Apples grow on trees in orchards.
An apple's seeds hide in the middle, in its core.
cards.didYouKnow: Apples float in water because they are full of tiny air pockets!

cards.front: Which yummy food is a patty inside a bun?
facts: A burger is a tasty patty served inside a soft bun.
Burgers are often made with beef, chicken or vegetables.
cards.didYouKnow: The burger is named after Hamburg, a city in Germany!

cards.front: Which food from Italy is made from wheat flour?
facts: Pasta comes from Italy.
It is made from wheat flour and water.
cards.didYouKnow: Spaghetti is a kind of pasta that is long and thin like strings!

cards.front: Which crispy pancake from South India is made from rice and lentils?
facts: A dosa is a crispy pancake from South India.
It is made from a batter of rice and lentils.
cards.didYouKnow: Dosa is eaten with sambar and coconut chutney!

cards.front: Which famous rice dish comes from India?
facts: Biryani is a tasty rice dish from India.
It is made with rice, spices, and meat or vegetables.
cards.didYouKnow: Biryani is cooked slowly so all the flavours mix together!

cards.front: Which snack pops when its kernels get hot?
facts: Popcorn is made from special corn kernels.
When the kernels get hot, they pop open into fluffy white pieces.
cards.didYouKnow: Popcorn is a favourite snack at the cinema!

cards.front: What is the capital of India?

Tigers have stripes just like human fingerprints — no two tigers have the same stripes.

It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

cards.didYouKnow: A peacock's tail can be more than 1.5 metres long.

Only male peacocks have the big colourful tail with eye-like spots.

cards.didYouKnow: A lotus flower closes at night and opens again in the morning.
facts: The lotus is the national flower of India.
It grows in muddy water but its petals always stay clean.
cards.front: Which flower is the national flower of India?

cards.didYouKnow: The Alphonso mango is called the king of mangoes.
facts: The mango is the national fruit of India.
India grows more mangoes than any other country in the world.
cards.front: Which fruit is the national fruit of India?
Which famous gate stands in New Delhi?
facts: It was built to honour the Indian soldiers who died in wars.
It is 42 metres tall, and the names of soldiers are written on its walls.
cards.didYouKnow: India Gate was built almost 100 years ago, in 1931.

cards.front: Which tall mountains stand in the north of India?
facts: The Himalayas are the tallest mountains in the world.
Mount Everest, the tallest mountain on Earth, is part of the Himalayas.
cards.didYouKnow: Himalaya means 'home of snow' in Sanskrit.

cards.front: What do we call the rainy season in India?
facts: The monsoon brings rain to India from June to September.
Farmers wait for the monsoon rain to grow their crops.
cards.didYouKnow: The word monsoon comes from an Arabic word that means 'season'.

cards.front: Which big animal with a long trunk is loved in India?
facts: Indian elephants have smaller ears than African elephants.
An elephant eats about 150 kg of leaves and grass in a day.
cards.didYouKnow: Elephants love to play in water and spray themselves with their trunks.

cards.front: Which snake spreads its hood wide when it is scared?
facts: When it feels scared, the cobra spreads its hood to look big.
A cobra's bite has venom, so we must stay far away from it.
cards.didYouKnow: The Indian cobra is one of the four most venomous snakes in India.

cards.front: Which exercise from India helps our body and mind stay calm?
facts: Yoga began in India thousands of years ago.
People all over the world do yoga to stay fit and calm.
cards.didYouKnow: 21st June is celebrated as International Yoga Day.

cards.front: Which game do most children in India love to play with a bat and ball?
facts: A cricket team has 11 players.
The game is played with a wooden bat and a hard ball.
cards.didYouKnow: Cricket came to India from England long ago.

cards.front: Which stick game did India win 8 Olympic gold medals in?
facts: India has won 8 gold medals in hockey at the Olympics.
Hockey is played with a stick and a small hard ball.
cards.didYouKnow: Major Dhyan Chand, a great hockey player, is called the Wizard of Hockey.

cards.front: Which tall tower in Delhi is made of red stone?
facts: It is 73 metres tall and was built about 800 years ago.
There are 379 steps inside it that go up to the top.
cards.didYouKnow: The Qutub Minar is one of the tallest brick towers in the world.

cards.front: Which famous building with four tall towers stands in Hyderabad?
facts: It was built more than 400 years ago, in 1591.
It has four tall towers called minarets.
cards.didYouKnow: Charminar means 'four towers'.

cards.front: Which big arch stands by the sea in Mumbai?
facts: It was built to welcome a king who visited India in 1911.
It stands on the shore of the Arabian Sea in Mumbai.
cards.didYouKnow: The Gateway of India is 26 metres tall.

cards.front: Which temple in Delhi looks like a lotus flower?
facts: It is shaped like a big white lotus flower.
People of all religions are welcome to pray there.
cards.didYouKnow: The Lotus Temple has nine sides, like the petals of a flower.

cards.front: Which holy place in Amritsar shines with gold?
facts: Its dome is covered with real gold.
It is the holiest place for Sikhs.
cards.didYouKnow: Free food is served to everyone who visits, in a hall called the langar.

cards.front: Which river flows past the Taj Mahal?
facts: The Yamuna flows through Delhi and past the Taj Mahal in Agra.
It joins the river Ganga at Prayagraj.
cards.didYouKnow: The Yamuna is the longest river that joins the Ganga.

cards.front: Which sea is on the west side of India?
facts: Mumbai and Goa are on the shore of the Arabian Sea.
The Arabian Sea is part of the big Indian Ocean.
cards.didYouKnow: Ships have sailed on the Arabian Sea for thousands of years.

cards.front: Which tree grows near the sea and gives us coconut?
facts: We drink sweet water from inside a green coconut.
Coconut is used in cooking in many parts of India.
cards.didYouKnow: A coconut tree can live for 60 to 80 years.

cards.front: Which yellow fruit grows in big bunches in India?
facts: Bananas grow in big bunches on a banana plant.
A banana gives us quick energy and is good for health.
cards.didYouKnow: India grows more bananas than any other country in the world.

cards.front: Which food do many people in India eat every day?
facts: Rice grows in fields filled with water, called paddy fields.
India is one of the largest growers of rice in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: Cooked rice is eaten with dal and vegetables in many Indian homes.

cards.front: Which train runs in big cities, sometimes under the ground?
facts: Metro trains run in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and many other cities.
Lakhs of people travel by metro every day.
cards.didYouKnow: The Kolkata Metro was the first metro train in India.

cards.front: Which small three-wheel vehicle takes us around Indian cities?
facts: An auto rickshaw has three wheels and a small roof.
It is a quick way to travel short distances in a city.
cards.didYouKnow: Auto rickshaws are also called tuk-tuks.

cards.front: Which small lamp do we light on Diwali?
facts: A diya is a small lamp made of clay.
We fill it with oil and light it on Diwali, the festival of lights.
cards.didYouKnow: People light diyas to show that light wins over darkness.

cards.front: Which colourful picture do we draw at the door during festivals?
facts: Rangoli is made with colourful powders and flowers.
People make rangoli to welcome guests and good luck.
cards.didYouKnow: Rangoli is also called kolam in Tamil Nadu.

cards.front: Which long cloth do many women in India wear?
facts: A sari is a long cloth, about five metres long.
It is worn in different ways in different parts of India.
cards.didYouKnow: Saris can be made of silk, cotton and many other materials.

cards.front: On which day do we celebrate Republic Day?
facts: On this day in 1950, the Constitution of India came into effect.
A big parade is held in New Delhi on Republic Day.
cards.didYouKnow: On Republic Day, the President of India unfurls the national flag in New Delhi.

cards.didYouKnow: Mumbai was once called Bombay.

It is also the financial capital of India.

cards.didYouKnow: Gandhi's full name was Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi.
facts: Mahatma Gandhi led India to freedom with non-violence.
His birthday, 2nd October, is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti.
cards.front: Who is called the Father of the Nation in India?

cards.didYouKnow: Kaziranga is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts: Kaziranga National Park is in Assam.
It is home to the largest number of one-horned rhinos in the world.
cards.front: Which national park is famous for one-horned rhinos?

cards.didYouKnow: National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February, the day he discovered the Raman Effect.
facts: C. V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.
He discovered why the sea looks blue — the Raman Effect.
cards.front: Who won India's first Nobel Prize in Science?

cards.didYouKnow: The Vande Bharat Express is one of India's fastest trains.
facts: Indian Railways runs more than 13,000 trains every day.
It has over 7,000 stations across the country.
cards.front: Which is one of the largest railway networks in the world?
Which classical dance comes from North India and is known for fast footwork?
facts: Kathak dancers wear ankle bells called ghungroos.
The dance tells stories with fast spins and hand movements.
cards.didYouKnow: The word Kathak comes from 'katha', which means story.

cards.front: Which game was born in India long ago and is played on a board with 64 squares?
facts: Chess began in India about 1,500 years ago as a game called chaturanga.
It is played by two players with 16 pieces each.
cards.didYouKnow: The word 'checkmate' comes from the Persian words 'shah mat', which mean 'the king is dead'.

cards.front: Which Indian team game is played by raiding the other side while holding your breath?
facts: A raider must chant 'kabaddi' while trying to touch the other players.
India has won the Kabaddi World Cup three times.
cards.didYouKnow: Kabaddi is one of the oldest games of India and is played in villages and cities.

cards.front: Which old university in India was one of the first in the world?
facts: Nalanda is in Bihar and is more than 1,500 years old.
Students from China and Korea came to Nalanda to study.
cards.didYouKnow: Nalanda had thousands of students and teachers, and a huge library.

cards.front: Which Indian mathematician first explained zero as a number?
facts: Brahmagupta lived about 1,400 years ago in the 7th century.
He wrote a famous book about maths and the stars.
cards.didYouKnow: Without zero, we could not write big numbers like 100 or 1,000.

cards.front: Which ancient Indian doctor is called the Father of Surgery?
facts: Sushruta lived more than 2,000 years ago in India.
He wrote a book about surgery and how to heal wounds.
cards.didYouKnow: Sushruta even described how to repair a nose by surgery.

cards.front: Which Indian mathematician amazed the world with his number theories?
facts: Ramanujan was a genius who loved numbers from a young age.
He went to Cambridge in England and worked with the famous mathematician G. H. Hardy.
cards.didYouKnow: Ramanujan died when he was only 32, but his work is still used by scientists today.

cards.front: Who wrote the Arthashastra and guided the Mauryan king Chandragupta?
facts: Chanakya was a teacher and a clever thinker.
He helped Chandragupta Maurya build the Mauryan Empire.
cards.didYouKnow: Chanakya is also called Kautilya.

cards.front: Which Mauryan king spread the message of peace after the Kalinga war?
facts: After the Kalinga war, Ashoka chose peace and Buddhism.
The lion capital of Ashoka is India's national emblem.
cards.didYouKnow: The wheel in the middle of the Indian flag is called the Ashoka Chakra.

cards.front: Which great warrior king built forts in Maharashtra?
facts: Shivaji built many strong forts in the hills of Maharashtra.
He was crowned king in 1674 at Raigad Fort.
cards.didYouKnow: Shivaji was a master of guerrilla warfare, fighting with speed and surprise.

cards.front: Which brave queen of Jhansi fought in the revolt of 1857?
facts: Rani Lakshmibai led her soldiers against the British in 1857.
She died fighting in battle in 1858.
cards.didYouKnow: Rani Lakshmibai is remembered as a symbol of bravery in India.

cards.front: Which young freedom fighter is remembered for his bravery at the age of 23?
facts: Bhagat Singh fought for India's freedom from British rule.
He was only 23 years old when he died in 1931.
cards.didYouKnow: Bhagat Singh's famous slogan was 'Inquilab Zindabad', which means 'Long live the revolution'.

cards.front: Who gave the famous call 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom'?
facts: Bose led the Indian National Army to free India.
He is lovingly called Netaji by the people of India.
cards.didYouKnow: Netaji's army had a women's unit called the Rani of Jhansi Regiment.

cards.front: Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
facts: Nehru was India's first Prime Minister after independence.
He loved children, and children called him Chacha Nehru.
cards.didYouKnow: Nehru's birthday, 14th November, is celebrated as Children's Day in India.

cards.front: Which kind lady served the poor in Kolkata and won the Nobel Peace Prize?
facts: Mother Teresa started the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata in 1950.
She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.
cards.didYouKnow: Mother Teresa was given India's highest honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1980.

cards.front: Who was the first Indian-born woman to travel to space?
facts: Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal, Haryana.
She flew to space in 1997 on the Space Shuttle Columbia.
cards.didYouKnow: Kalpana Chawla died in 2003 when the Columbia broke apart on its way back to Earth.

cards.front: Which temple in Odisha is built like a huge chariot of the Sun God?
facts: It was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I.
The temple is shaped like a chariot with 24 stone wheels.
cards.didYouKnow: The wheels of the temple work as sundials and can tell the time.

cards.front: Which old city in Karnataka was once the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire?
facts: Hampi was the capital of the great Vijayanagara Empire.
It is famous for its stone chariot and old temples.
cards.didYouKnow: Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

cards.front: Which caves in Maharashtra have paintings that are more than 2,000 years old?
facts: There are about 30 caves at Ajanta.
The paintings on the walls tell stories of the Buddha.
cards.didYouKnow: The Ajanta Caves were lost in the forest for hundreds of years before they were found again.

cards.front: Which is one of the oldest cities in the world, on the banks of the Ganga?
facts: Varanasi is more than 3,000 years old.
It is famous for its ghats, where people pray on the banks of the Ganga.
cards.didYouKnow: Varanasi is also called Kashi and Banaras.

cards.front: Which mountain range runs along the west coast of India?
facts: The Western Ghats run through Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
They are home to many plants and animals found nowhere else in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

cards.front: Which river in Assam is one of the biggest in India?
facts: The Brahmaputra flows through Tibet, India and Bangladesh.
It forms Majuli, the largest river island in the world.
cards.didYouKnow: In Tibet, the Brahmaputra is called the Tsangpo.

cards.front: What is the name of the lower house of the Indian Parliament?
facts: The Lok Sabha has 543 members chosen by the people.
Its members are elected every five years.
cards.didYouKnow: Lok Sabha means 'House of the People'.

cards.front: Which is the highest court in India?
facts: The Supreme Court is in New Delhi.
It protects the Constitution and the rights of the people.
cards.didYouKnow: The decisions of the Supreme Court must be followed by all other courts in India.

cards.front: Which is the largest mangrove forest in the world?
Which ancient city gives its name to the Harappan civilisation?
facts: Harappa is in present-day Pakistan and was found in the 1920s.
The Harappan civilisation is about 4,500 years old.
cards.didYouKnow: Harappan cities had planned streets, drains and even bathrooms.

cards.front: Which period of Indian history is called the Golden Age?
facts: The Gupta Age lasted from about 320 to 550 CE.
Great minds like Aryabhata and Kalidasa lived in this age.
cards.didYouKnow: Art, science and literature grew fast during the Gupta Age.

cards.front: Which company came to India to trade and later ruled much of the country?
facts: The company came to India in 1600 to trade in spices and cloth.
After the revolt of 1857, the British Crown took over its rule in 1858.
cards.didYouKnow: The company had its own army and ruled India for about 100 years.

cards.front: Which march in 1930 protested the British tax on salt?
facts: Gandhiji walked about 385 km from Sabarmati to Dandi in 24 days.
At Dandi, he broke the salt law by making salt from sea water.
cards.didYouKnow: Thousands of people joined Gandhiji on the march to Dandi.

cards.front: Which part of the Constitution begins with 'We the People of India'?
facts: The Preamble tells the aims of the Constitution.
It promises Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity to all citizens.
cards.didYouKnow: The Preamble is called the soul of the Constitution.

cards.front: How many fundamental rights does the Indian Constitution give its citizens?
facts: The six rights include the Right to Equality and the Right to Freedom.
If a right is taken away, a citizen can go to the court for help.
cards.didYouKnow: The Right to Education for children aged 6 to 14 is a fundamental right.

cards.front: What is the name of the single tax that replaced many taxes in 2017?
facts: GST began on 1st July 2017.
It joined many taxes into one tax for the whole country.
cards.didYouKnow: GST is also called 'One Nation, One Tax'.

cards.front: Which body conducts elections in India?
facts: The Election Commission was set up in 1950.
It makes sure elections in India are free and fair.
cards.didYouKnow: India's elections are the largest in the world, with nearly 100 crore voters.

cards.front: Which hills in South India are called the Blue Mountains?
facts: The Nilgiri Hills are in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.
Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiris, at 2,637 metres.
cards.didYouKnow: Nilgiri means 'blue mountains' because the hills look blue from far away.

cards.front: Which river flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges?
facts: The Narmada flows to the west and falls into the Arabian Sea.
It is one of the few Indian rivers that flow to the west.
cards.didYouKnow: The Narmada is one of the seven holy rivers of India.

cards.front: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
facts: Wular Lake is in Jammu and Kashmir.
It is fed by the river Jhelum.
cards.didYouKnow: Wular Lake changes its size with the seasons — it grows big in the monsoon.

cards.front: Which is the oldest national park in India?
facts: It was set up in 1936 in Uttarakhand.
It is famous for the Bengal tiger.
cards.didYouKnow: The park was first called Hailey National Park.

cards.front: Which project started in 1973 to save tigers in India?
facts: Project Tiger began with 9 tiger reserves.
Today India has more than 50 tiger reserves.
cards.didYouKnow: The number of tigers in India has more than doubled since 2006.

cards.front: Which mission made India the first Asian country to reach Mars?
facts: Mangalyaan reached Mars in 2014.
India was the first country to reach Mars on its very first try.
cards.didYouKnow: Mangalyaan cost less than many Hollywood films.

cards.front: Which mission studies the Sun from space?
facts: Aditya-L1 was launched in 2023.
It studies the Sun from a special point in space called L1.
cards.didYouKnow: Aditya is another name for the Sun God.

cards.front: Which ancient Indian mathematician wrote the Aryabhatiya?
facts: Aryabhata lived about 1,500 years ago.
He explained that the Earth spins on its axis and worked out the length of the year.
cards.didYouKnow: India's first satellite was named Aryabhata in his honour.

cards.front: Who is called the Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme?
facts: Homi Bhabha set up the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.

cards.didYouKnow: Homi Bhabha dreamed that India would use atomic energy for peace.

cards.front: Which Buddhist stupa was built by Emperor Ashoka?
facts: It is in Madhya Pradesh and was built in the 3rd century BCE.
It is one of the oldest stone buildings in India.
cards.didYouKnow: The four gateways of the stupa are carved with stories from the life of the Buddha.

cards.front: Which palace in Jaipur is called the Palace of Winds?
facts: It was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh.
It has 953 small windows, called jharokhas.
cards.didYouKnow: The palace was built so royal women could watch festivals in the street without being seen.

cards.front: Which gathering is the largest religious gathering in the world?
facts: The Kumbh Mela is held in turn at Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik and Ujjain.
More than 100 million people came to the Kumbh in Prayagraj in 2013.
cards.didYouKnow: The Kumbh Mela is so big that it can be seen from space.

cards.front: Which classical dance comes from Andhra Pradesh?
facts: Kuchipudi began in a village of the same name in Andhra Pradesh.
Dancers tell stories with fast footwork and face expressions.
cards.didYouKnow: In Kuchipudi, dancers sometimes dance on the rim of a brass plate.

cards.front: Who was the chief architect of the Indian Constitution?
facts: Dr. Ambedkar led the team that wrote the Constitution.
He fought all his life for the rights of the oppressed.
cards.didYouKnow: Dr. Ambedkar's birthday, 14th April, is celebrated as Ambedkar Jayanti.

cards.front: Who spoke at the World Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893?
facts: Vivekananda began his speech with 'Sisters and brothers of America'.
He founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.
cards.didYouKnow: Vivekananda's speech in Chicago made him famous all over the world.

cards.front: Who won India's first Olympic gold medal in athletics?
facts: Neeraj Chopra won gold in javelin throw at the Tokyo Olympics.
He is from Haryana and was a soldier in the Indian Army.
cards.didYouKnow: Neeraj Chopra's winning throw went 87.58 metres.

Her story is about justice — she fought for her husband, Kovalan.
cards.front: Who is the heroine of the Tamil epic Silappatikaram?

cards.didYouKnow: The Vaigai river is named in many old Tamil poems.
facts: The Vaigai flows through Madurai in southern Tamil Nadu.
It joins the sea in the Palk Strait.
cards.front: Which river flows through Madurai?

cards.didYouKnow: The Tamirabharani never dries up, even in summer.
facts: The Tamirabharani starts in the Western Ghats.
It flows through Tirunelveli and reaches the sea near Thoothukudi.
cards.front: Which river flows through Tirunelveli?

cards.didYouKnow: The Palk Strait is so shallow in some places that you can almost walk across at low tide.
facts: The Palk Strait separates Tamil Nadu from Sri Lanka.
It is named after Robert Palk, a British governor of Madras.
cards.front: Which sea strait lies between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka?

cards.didYouKnow: The Gulf of Mannar was India's first marine biosphere reserve.
facts: The Gulf of Mannar lies between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka.
It is home to coral reefs, sea cows and pearl oysters.
cards.front: Which gulf between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka is famous for corals and pearls?

cards.didYouKnow: Mangrove trees grow in salty water, and their roots protect the coast from big waves.
facts: Pichavaram is a mangrove forest near Chidambaram.
Boats take visitors through its quiet green water channels.
cards.front: Which mangrove forest near Chidambaram is one of the largest in India?

cards.didYouKnow: The Srirangam temple is so big that a small town with streets and houses sits inside its walls.
facts: The Srirangam temple covers about 156 acres.
It has 21 tall towers called gopurams.
cards.front: Which temple in Trichy is one of the largest temple complexes in the world?

cards.didYouKnow: Dancers from all over India come to Chidambaram for the Natyanjali dance festival.
facts: The Nataraja Temple in Chidambaram shows Shiva dancing in a golden hall.
It is one of the five Pancha Bhoota Sthalams, for the element of space.
cards.front: Which temple is famous for Lord Shiva as the dancing Nataraja?

cards.didYouKnow: Yercaud is called the Poor Man's Ooty because it is pretty like Ooty but less crowded.
facts: Yercaud is a hill station in the Shevaroy Hills near Salem.
Its lake is called the Emerald Lake.
cards.front: Which hill station near Salem is famous for its lake?

cards.didYouKnow: The Crocodile Bank was started by Romulus Whitaker, a famous snake expert.
facts: The Crocodile Bank is near Mamallapuram, south of Chennai.
It looks after many kinds of crocodiles and snakes.
cards.front: Which famous centre near Mamallapuram protects crocodiles?

cards.didYouKnow: At Thiruchendur, the sea waves touch the temple walls.
facts: Thiruchendur is one of the six holy homes of Lord Murugan.
It is the only Murugan temple that stands right on the sea shore.
cards.front: Which Murugan temple stands on the sea shore?

cards.didYouKnow: Karagattam is performed to honour Mariamman, the goddess of rain.
facts: Karagattam is a traditional dance of Tamil Nadu.
Dancers balance a decorated pot on their head while dancing.
cards.front: In which Tamil dance do dancers balance a pot on their head?

cards.didYouKnow: The Thirukkural has been translated into many languages around the world.
facts: Thiruvalluvar wrote the Thirukkural more than 2,000 years ago.
It has 1,330 short poems about life, love and good conduct.
cards.front: Who wrote the Thirukkural?

cards.didYouKnow: The temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts: Raja Raja Chola built the Brihadeeswara Temple about 1,000 years ago.
Its tower is made of granite stone and is about 66 metres tall.
cards.front: Which great temple did Raja Raja Chola build in Thanjavur?

cards.didYouKnow: Periyar's birthday, 17 September, is celebrated as Social Justice Day in Tamil Nadu.
facts: Periyar worked for social reform and equality in Tamil Nadu.
He started the Self-Respect Movement.
cards.front: Who is known as Periyar?

cards.didYouKnow: Marina Beach is about 13 km long.
facts: Marina Beach is in Chennai.
It is one of the longest urban beaches in the world.
cards.front: Which is the longest natural urban beach in India?

cards.didYouKnow: Rajendra Chola's navy sailed all the way to Southeast Asia.
facts: Gangaikonda Cholapuram was built by Rajendra Chola I around 1025 CE.
Its temple is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
cards.front: Which city did Rajendra Chola build as his capital?

cards.didYouKnow: Thanjavur paintings are protected with a GI tag.
facts: Thanjavur paintings use gold foil and bright colours.
They often show gods and goddesses.
cards.front: Which famous painting style comes from Thanjavur?

cards.didYouKnow: Rajendra Chola's navy even reached the kingdom of Srivijaya in 1025 CE.
facts: The Cholas built strong ships and had a powerful navy.
Their ships sailed to South-East Asia, to places like Malaysia and Indonesia.
cards.front: Which Tamil dynasty had a powerful navy that sailed to South-East Asia?

cards.didYouKnow: Chola bronze statues are made using the lost-wax method, which is more than 4,000 years old.
facts: Chola bronze statues are famous all over the world.
The dancing Shiva, or Nataraja, is the most famous Chola bronze.
cards.front: Which dynasty made the world-famous bronze statue of dancing Shiva?

cards.didYouKnow: Keezhadi shows that Tamil people lived in towns with brick houses and drainage more than 2,500 years ago.
facts: Keezhadi is an excavation site near Madurai.
Artefacts found there are from the 6th century BCE, more than 2,500 years ago.
cards.front: Which excavation near Madurai found Tamil artefacts more than 2,500 years old?

cards.didYouKnow: Sangam poems talk about love, war, kings, farming and the sea.
facts: Sangam literature is the oldest Tamil writing.
It was written more than 2,000 years ago by Tamil poets.
cards.front: What is the oldest Tamil writing called?

cards.didYouKnow: Tolkappiyam also teaches poets how to write poems about love and war.
facts: Tolkappiyam is the oldest Tamil grammar book.
It was written more than 2,000 years ago.
cards.front: What is the oldest Tamil grammar book called?

cards.didYouKnow: Manimekalai was written by Seethalai Sattanar, a Tamil poet.
facts: Manimekalai is one of the five great Tamil epics.
Its heroine feeds the hungry with a magic bowl called Amudhasurabhi.
cards.front: Which Tamil epic tells of a woman who feeds the hungry with a magic bowl?

cards.didYouKnow: Dravidian architecture began more than 1,300 years ago under the Pallava kings.
facts: The great temples of Tamil Nadu are built in the Dravidian style.
Dravidian temples have tall towers called gopurams and pillared halls.
cards.front: In which style are the great temples of Tamil Nadu built?

cards.didYouKnow: The carving tells the story of the river Ganga coming down to Earth.
facts: The Descent of the Ganges is a huge rock carving at Mamallapuram.
It is about 29 metres long and 13 metres high.
cards.front: Which giant rock carving at Mamallapuram is one of the largest in the world?

cards.didYouKnow: The Five Rathas were carved in the 7th century, more than 1,300 years ago.
facts: The Five Rathas at Mamallapuram are five temples carved from single rocks.
Each ratha is named after a hero of the Mahabharata.
cards.front: Which five temples at Mamallapuram are each carved from a single rock?

cards.didYouKnow: The temple is built of sandstone and has small shrines all around its walls.
facts: The Kailasanathar Temple was built about 1,300 years ago.
It was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II.
cards.front: Which is the oldest temple in Kanchipuram?

cards.didYouKnow: The temple has stone steps that sing like musical notes when you tap them.
facts: The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was built by Rajaraja Chola II.
It is one of the three Great Living Chola Temples on the UNESCO list.
cards.front: Which Chola temple at Darasuram is on the UNESCO World Heritage list?

cards.didYouKnow: Kattabomman is remembered as one of the first Tamil freedom fighters.
facts: Kattabomman was the ruler of Panchalankurichi.
He refused to pay taxes to the British and fought them.
cards.front: Which Tamil king fought the British and was hanged in 1799?

cards.didYouKnow: Dheeran Chinnamalai was hanged by the British in 1805.
facts: Dheeran Chinnamalai was a freedom fighter from Kongu Nadu.
He fought the British in three battles at Cauvery, Odanilai and Arachalur.
cards.front: Which freedom fighter from Kongu Nadu fought the British?

cards.didYouKnow: The Marudhu brothers gave shelter to Veerapandiya Kattabomman's family.
facts: The Marudhu brothers, Periya Marudhu and Chinna Marudhu, ruled Sivaganga.
They fought the British and were hanged in 1801.
cards.front: Which two brothers were freedom fighters from Sivaganga?

cards.didYouKnow: Kumaran is called Kodi Katha Kumaran, which means Kumaran who protected the flag.
facts: Tiruppur Kumaran was a freedom fighter from Tiruppur.
He died in 1932 while holding the Indian flag in a protest.
cards.front: Which freedom fighter died holding the Indian flag in 1932?

cards.didYouKnow: Jayalalithaa was called Amma, which means mother, by her supporters.
facts: Jayalalithaa was a famous film actor before she entered politics.
She was the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu six times.
cards.front: Which actor became the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu?

cards.didYouKnow: Greek and Roman writers wrote about the pearls of Korkai more than 2,000 years ago.
facts: Korkai was an ancient port of the Pandya kings.
It was famous for pearl fishing long ago.
cards.front: Which ancient Pandya port was famous for pearls?

cards.didYouKnow: The Vellore Mutiny happened 51 years before the great revolt of 1857.
facts: The Vellore Mutiny happened in 1806 at Vellore Fort.
Indian soldiers rose against the British, many years before the revolt of 1857.
cards.front: Which revolt in 1806 was one of the first against British rule in India?

cards.didYouKnow: The Western Ghats are older than the Himalaya mountains.
facts: The Western Ghats run along the western side of Tamil Nadu.
They are one of the world's richest places for plants and animals.
cards.front: Which mountain range runs along Tamil Nadu and is a UNESCO World Heritage site?

cards.didYouKnow: Vedanthangal has been protected as a bird sanctuary since 1798.
facts: Vedanthangal is near Chennai in Tamil Nadu.
Thousands of birds from faraway countries come here every year.
cards.front: Which is one of the oldest bird sanctuaries in India?

cards.didYouKnow: A classical language is one with a very old and rich literature.
facts: Tamil was declared a classical language in 2004.
It was the first Indian language to get this honour.
cards.front: Which was the first Indian language declared a classical language?

cards.didYouKnow: The dam helps farmers water their fields in Erode district.
facts: Bhavanisagar Dam is built on the Bhavani river near Sathyamangalam.
It is one of the largest earthen dams in the world.
cards.front: Which dam in Tamil Nadu is one of the largest earthen dams in the world?

cards.didYouKnow: Kalpakkam also has a research centre where scientists study atoms.
facts: Kalpakkam has the Madras Atomic Power Station.
The power station makes electricity from nuclear energy.
cards.front: Which town near Chennai has a nuclear power plant?

cards.didYouKnow: The library was started by the Nayak kings and made famous by the Maratha king Serfoji II.
facts: The Saraswathi Mahal Library is in Thanjavur.
It has thousands of old palm-leaf manuscripts in Tamil and Sanskrit.
cards.front: Which library in Thanjavur is one of the oldest in Asia?
